name: Waxwing Neuromedia
sovereign_territory: Waxwing Spire District — a 3.2 square kilometer enclave in central Chicago's former Streeterville neighborhood, dominated by the 94-story Waxwing Spire tower and a subterranean server complex nicknamed The Hive, extending 11 stories below the water table
founding_story: Waxwing was incorporated in 2147 by neuroscientist-turned-media theorist Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran and her business partner, former streaming executive Tomás Reinholt, following their breakthrough in 'cognitive addressable content' — entertainment delivered directly via neural interface that adapts in real time to the viewer's emotional and neurochemical state. Their founding pitch was simple and terrifying: 'We don't make content you watch. We make content you feel from the inside.' The corponation grew explosively as neural interface adoption rates in GLMZ crossed 60% of the adult population by 2153.
security_force: Waxwing Perceptual Security (WPS), a 4,200-person force notable for its use of proprietary 'cognitive disruption' non-lethal weapons that temporarily overwhelm a target's sensory processing via their own neural interface. Physical security is considered secondary; Waxwing's primary defensive posture is informational — the corponation maintains dossiers on the neural consumption patterns of virtually every person in GLMZ, providing extraordinary leverage.
key_detail: Waxwing's advertising division, operating under the subsidiary brand CANDOR, holds a Meridian Corridor license to deliver 'subthreshold cognitive impressions' — advertisements embedded below conscious awareness directly into neural feeds. The practice is technically legal under a 2155 Corridor Council ruling that Waxwing itself drafted the language for. Civil liberties groups have been filing injunctions continuously for nine years. None have succeeded.
relationship_to_big_20: Full Big 20 member, ranked approximately 7th by influence metrics. Has a deeply adversarial relationship with MIRRORWELL MEDIA, which operates in overlapping entertainment sectors but uses traditional screen-based delivery. The two corponations have engaged in three formal economic warfare declarations since 2158, each resolved by Corridor Council arbitration that both parties publicly accepted and privately ignored.
full_text: Waxwing Neuromedia Sovereign Corponation — stock designation WXWG-NM — is the GLMZ corridor's dominant force in direct neural entertainment and cognitive advertising, operating from the Waxwing Spire District, a 3.2 square kilometer sovereign enclave carved from Chicago's former Streeterville neighborhood. The 94-story Waxwing Spire and its 11-level subterranean server complex known as The Hive together house the infrastructure for a media empire valued at Φ890 billion Meridian Script, generating Φ134 billion in annual revenue from 29,000 direct employees and 400,000 registered content architects who build experiences for the platform. Founded in 2147 by Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran and Tomás Reinholt following their breakthrough in cognitive addressable content — entertainment that enters directly through neural interfaces and reshapes itself around the viewer's live emotional and neurochemical state — Waxwing grew from a provocative startup to a sovereign power in under a decade, riding the wave of neural interface adoption that crossed 60% of GLMZ adults by 2153. Its security arm, Waxwing Perceptual Security, fields 4,200 personnel equipped with cognitive disruption weapons that turn a target's own neural interface against them, but the corponation's true defensive arsenal is informational: Waxwing maintains granular neural consumption profiles on virtually every interfaced person in the corridor. Its advertising subsidiary CANDOR operates under a Corridor Council license — written by Waxwing's own legal team — permitting subthreshold cognitive impressions, advertisements delivered below conscious awareness directly into the feed. The license has been under continuous legal challenge for nine years. Waxwing remains a full Big 20 member, ranked near the top of influence metrics, and sustains a grinding economic cold war with MIRRORWELL MEDIA that has required three separate Corridor Council interventions, all of which both parties have decorated with compliance and disregarded in practice.
